narrative_purpose: Makes the chapter's hinge visible: two trees too far apart for their roots to ever touch — the roots reaching out and falling short across a gap — while a far finer web of fungal threads quietly bridges the void between them, resolving the paradox that roots alone could never wire a planet.
subject: Two large trees separated by a wide gap of soil, their thick roots reaching toward each other but clearly stopping short, a visible empty span between the two root systems; threading across that gap, far finer and almost invisible, a delicate web of glowing fungal filaments that actually connects the two, doing the job the roots cannot.
scene: An underground cross-section beneath two trees with a stream or rocky barrier on the surface above the gap, emphasising the distance the roots cannot cross.
camera: A wide side-on cross-section showing both trees and the full gap between their roots.
light: Dim earthy ambient above; the thick roots rendered solid and unlit, the fine fungal bridge glowing faint cyan as the only luminous element across the gap.
palette: Deep void-indigo soil, muted brown-grey roots, vivid but delicate Pandora cyan only on the fungal threads bridging the void.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate with diagrammatic clarity, hand-painted texture.
detail_level: Crisp on the two root systems and the failing gap between them; the fungal bridge fine and luminous; surroundings soft.
composition: Two trees at left and right edges, a deliberately wide dark gap centred between their roots, the thin glowing bridge crossing it, generous dark space for labels.
consistency_notes: Earth-science/Pandora-bridging figure in the book's cool palette; the contrast between thick-but-short roots and fine-but-far-reaching fungus must read instantly; leave dark space for callout labels.
